proposed.sourceName: US FDA — 21 CFR §101.22(a)(3), definition of natural flavor
proposed.paraphrase: The US federal definition of 'natural flavor' permits derivation from 'meat, seafood, poultry, eggs, dairy products, or fermentation products thereof' as well as plant material, without disclosing the specific constituents — so the source could include non-zabiha animal material and cannot be confirmed halal from the label.

proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation — Halal Certification for Natural & Artificial Flavors
proposed.paraphrase: The American Halal Foundation states natural flavors are not halal by default: flavors from haram animal sources or animal derivatives are haram, and ethanol-extracted flavors above 5000 ppm residuals are haram; verification of source and process is required.

researcherNote: Zabiha (strictest) position. An undisclosed possibly-animal source cannot meet the zabiha verification bar, so it is avoided pending certification -> seeded draft grade 4 (Questionable - widely avoided). Two independent tier-1 sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-06-28.
